function.description:
Retrieves the count (number) of rule-based compliance (RBC) policies configured in Catalyst Center. Use this for ANY 'how many' / count / total-number question about compliance/RBC policies. ALWAYS prefer this over listing policies and counting them: the list tool (api_getCompliancePolicies) is page-size limited (defaults to 10 and rejects large limits), so counting its returned items is inaccurate whenever more than one page exists. For 'how many compliance policies apply to <site>?', resolve the site's `id` with api_getSites first and pass it as `siteId`; that count is the site's effective total and includes policies inherited from ancestor sites such as Global. The `name` filter matches POLICY names only — never pass a site name to it. This counts configured compliance policies, NOT the number of compliant/non-compliant devices.

Partial filters: this tool can only narrow the count by `name` and `siteId`. If the user asks for a count narrowed by anything else — the state of a policy, the rules or conditions it contains, the device types it applies to — still return the count with the filters that ARE supported, and say plainly which part of the request could not be applied, for example "there are N compliance policies for that site; I can't narrow that by <filter> because the count API has no parameter for it." Never present a partially filtered count as though the unsupported filter had been applied, and never approximate the missing filter by listing policies and tallying them, because the list tool is paginated.
function.name: api_getCompliancePolicyCount

name.description: Filter by compliance policy name. The match is exact and case-sensitive: the value must be the policy's complete stored name, so a partial name, an extra word, a keyword, or different capitalisation returns nothing. Pass `name` only when you already have that exact name, typically because the user quoted it. Do not assemble a value out of the user's own phrasing, and remember that a trailing 'policy' or 'compliance policy' is usually not part of the stored name. When the user describes a policy loosely, resolve it first with api_getCompliancePolicies called without `name`, then use the exact name from that listing. MANDATORY: if a call with `name` returns zero, resolve the name that way before answering. A zero count for a filtered call only means nothing matched that exact string, so never conclude from it that the policy does not exist.

policyId.description: The IDs of the compliance policies.

siteId.description: The `id` of the site to which compliance policies are associated.

responses.description: Reports a count, for example, a total count of records in a given resource.
responses.title: Count Response
